newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo banks report 70 mln dinar losses in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Yugo banks report 70 mln dinar losses in 1996.

text.p: Yugoslavia's ailing banks reported on Thursday 70 million dinars ($12.15 million) in losses for 1996 while their unrecoverable claims more than doubled.
This compared to the banking sector's total losses of $19.7 million in 1995 and $94.4 million in 1994.

"An important reason for negative results is a large amount of unrecoverable claims which grew to 3.5 billion dinars at the end of 1996," general secretary of the Yugoslav Banking Association (YBA) Mileta Babovic told YBA's annual meeting.
According to YBA statistics, bad debts rose to 3.5 billion dinars from 1.5 billion at the end of 1995.
"Unrecoverable claims result first of all from weak financial position of debtors and overall illiquidity of companies and banks," Babovic said addressing the meeting.
Yugoslavia's internal indebtedness is a growing problem with inter-company debt, accumulated since 1994, reaching almost $7 billion.
